text: Day 1 at the Gull Point lighthouse. A steady west wind pushed grey clouds across the sky all day. Long swells rolled in from the open water and broke white on the rocks. A family of four came to see the lamp and asked many questions about the clockwork. The lens was cleaned with a soft cloth and a little vinegar water. The barometer read 1003 millibars at noon, and the keeper counted 10 gulls on the roof of the oil store. At sunset the lamp was lit, and the keeper watched the first ships pass.

Day 2 at the Gull Point lighthouse. Bright sunshine warmed the stone steps before noon. The tide ran unusually low, showing the green weed on the lower ledges. The postman brought two letters and a parcel of lamp wicks. Fresh oil was carried up in two trips and the reservoir was filled. The barometer read 1016 millibars at noon, and the keeper counted 17 gulls on the roof of the oil store. By evening everything was in order, and the beam swept the water as usual.
